  "what_the_study_did": "The study developed and validated a method for analyzing the concentration-QTc relationship in preclinical animal models using sparse pharmacokinetic data.",
  "what_it_found": "The proposed method accurately predicts QTc changes in animals based on drug concentration, correlating well with human data, and can be applied even with non-simultaneous PK and QTc measurements.",
  "key_quotes": [
    {
      "quote": "In NHP, a 10.9 ± 0.06 ms (mean ± 95% CI) change in QTc was detected at approximately 1.5× the moxifloxacin plasma concentration that causes a 10 ms QTc change in humans, based on a 0-24 h super-interval.",

      "topic": "Canine vs Human"
    },
    {
      "quote": "While simultaneous PK and QTc data points are preferred, practical constraints and the need for QTc averaging did not prevent concentration-QTc analyses.",
      "topic": "Data Pairing"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Utilizing a 0-24 h super-interval method illustrates a simple and effective method to address cardiovascular questions when preclinical drug exposures exceed clinical concentrations.",
      "topic": "Method Effectiveness"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Previous studies have confirmed that canine and NHP studies may be useful for predicting human outcomes.",
      "topic": "Translational Value"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Humans, however, are more sensitive, with their maximum probability of a QTc prolonging effect occurring at lower concentrations than in NHP and canine.",
      "topic": "Species Sensitivity"
    }
  ]
